motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing 10.A., 12.B., 13.C., and 13.D. and placing them on the regularly scheduled items for further discussion. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Approve routine items, pull four for debate
motions.summary: The council approved its batch of routine consent items, pulling four — including the civic campus land purchase and the QTS agreement — out for separate discussion.
motions.impact: This is routine housekeeping and nothing changes for residents. It only means four items got their own debate instead of passing quietly in a bundle.

motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to table Firefly 4MG Tank Change Order #2. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Delay a change order on the Firefly water tank
motions.summary: The council set aside a second change order for the Firefly 4MG tank rather than deciding it at this meeting.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents right now — the tank project's cost change is simply waiting for a future meeting.

motions.item_title: Approve the Verizon Pro Communications Tower Site Plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve the Verizon Pro Communications Tower Site Plan. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Approve a Verizon communications tower
motions.summary: The city signed off on the site plan for a Verizon communications tower, clearing the way for it to be built.
motions.impact: If you live near the site you will see a tower go up, though the motion doesn't say where it goes. For the rest of the city, nothing changes.

motions.item_title: A Resolution Approving the First Amendment to the QTS Eagle Mountain Development Agreement
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve a Resolution Approving the First Amendment to the QTS Eagle Mountain Development Agreement. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Amend the QTS development agreement
motions.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the city's development agreement with QTS; the motion does not state what the amendment changes.
motions.impact: Nothing in this motion points to a change residents would feel — it is a contract adjustment between the city and one developer. The specifics live in the amendment, not the motion.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Purchase Agreement with Ivory Homes and SITLA to purchase 20.99 acres of Land for a Future Civic Campus
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Purchase Agreement with Ivory Homes and SITLA to purchase 20.99 acres of Land for a Future Civic Campus. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Buy 21 acres for a future civic campus
motions.summary: The city approved an agreement with Ivory Homes and SITLA to buy 20.99 acres of land for a future civic campus.
motions.impact: This locks in the land for city buildings down the road. Nothing gets built yet — what goes on the site, and what it costs, would come back to the council separately.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 16 Related to the Water Rights and Concept Plans with changes as stated
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 16 Related to the Water Rights and Concept Plans with changes as stated. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Change water rules for new development
motions.summary: The city rewrote the part of its development code covering water rights and concept plans, adopting the change with amendments made during the meeting.
motions.impact: This lands on developers bringing new projects forward, who will have to meet the revised water-rights and concept-plan requirements. Nothing changes day to day for people already living here.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Sections 17.10.030, 17.20.020, 17.25.030, and 17.40.020
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Sections 17.10.030, 17.20.020, 17.25.030, and 17.40.020. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Four sections of the zoning code amended
motions.summary: The council amended four sections of the city's zoning code; the motion lists only the section numbers and does not say what the changes do.
motions.impact: There is nothing in this motion that tells a resident what actually changed — only section numbers. The substance is in the ordinance itself, not in what was voted on here.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.75; Standards for Special Uses - Outdoor Storage of Recreational Vehicles and Trailers as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.75; Standards for Special Uses - Outdoor Storage of Recreational Vehicles and Trailers as presented. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New rules for outdoor RV and trailer storage
motions.summary: The city rewrote the standards governing outdoor storage of recreational vehicles and trailers, updating the chapter of the code that treats it as a special use.
motions.impact: If you store an RV, boat, or trailer outdoors — or run a storage lot — the rules you follow have changed. The motion itself doesn't spell out how, so check the updated code chapter before you park.
